sections.heading: Lead
Content
sections.wikitext: The lyrics describe placing a call to someone in the middle of the night due to being lonely and longing for companionship. Hillary Scott commented on the song, saying that "All three of us know what it's like to get to that point where you feel lonely enough that you make a late-night phone call that you very well could regret the next day." Charles Kelley told ''The Boot'' that the band's record executives initially had concerns regarding using the lyrics ''"I'm a little drunk"'', but he convinced the executives to leave the content in the song.<ref name=songinfo>{{cite web|url=http://www.songfacts.com/detail.php?id=16541|title="Need You Now" song facts|access-date=September 26, 2010}}</ref>
sections.text: The lyrics describe placing a call to someone in the middle of the night due to being lonely and longing for companionship. Hillary Scott commented on the song, saying that "All three of us know what it's like to get to that point where you feel lonely enough that you make a late-night phone call that you very well could regret the next day." sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
David McClister directed the "Need You Now" [[music video]], using a treatment he wrote in 10 minutes.<ref name=davidmcclisterinterview>{{cite web|url=http://knowtheartist.com/david-mcclister/ |title=How David McClister shot LeAnn Rimes (in a music video) |publisher=KnowTheArtist.com |author=Armstrong, Josh |date=August 1, 2011 |access-date=August 16, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401030547/http://knowtheartist.com/david-mcclister/ |archive-date=April 1, 2012 }}</ref>

The video features all three members of Lady Antebellum acting out scenes pertaining to the storyline. It begins in a hallway of a hotel where Charles Kelley is sitting against a wall and Hillary Scott is in her room, with Dave Haywood playing the piano. Kelley goes to a cafe and has a coffee, where Haywood arrives with his love interest. Scott then leaves her room and hails a taxi. Kelley leaves the cafe and goes outside to walk to a costume ball, to which Scott is also traveling. When they arrive at the ball, they both see their love interests wearing masks and embrace them. Haywood soon arrives at the ball with his love interest. The video ends with all three members embracing their love interests.<ref name=musicvideo/> The video was filmed at the [[The Omni King Edward Hotel|King Edward Hotel]] in [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]].<ref name="weekly">{{cite journal|last=Paxman|first=Bob|date=September 28, 2009|title=Pulling an All-Nighter: Lady Antebellum's video shoot for "Need You Now" was an after-hours blast in Toronto.|journal=[[Country Weekly]]|volume=16|issue=33|page=25|issn=1074-3235}}</ref>

Of the changes between the song and its music video, one of the most noted is Kelley drinking coffee instead of whiskey, since the song states the character is intoxicated. In response, McClister admitted he simply did not want the video to be a literal adaptation of the song, as he felt sitting in a diner in the middle of the night was lonelier.<ref name=davidmcclisterinterview/>
sections.text:
David McClister directed the "Need You Now" music video, using a treatment he wrote in 10 minutes.

The video features all three members of Lady Antebellum acting out scenes pertaining to the storyline. It begins in a hallway of a hotel where Charles Kelley is sitting against a wall and Hillary Scott is in her room, with Dave Haywood playing the piano. Kelley goes to a cafe and has a coffee, where Haywood arrives with his love interest. Scott then leaves her room and hails a taxi. Kelley leaves the cafe and goes outside to walk to a costume ball, to which Scott is also traveling. When they arrive at the ball, they both see their love interests wearing masks and embrace them. Haywood soon arrives at the ball with his love interest. The video ends with all three members embracing their love interests. The video was filmed at the King Edward Hotel in Toronto, Ontario.

Of the changes between the song and its music video, one of the most noted is Kelley drinking coffee instead of whiskey, since the song states the character is intoxicated. In response, McClister admitted he simply did not want the video to be a literal adaptation of the song, as he felt sitting in a diner in the middle of the night was lonelier.

sections.heading: Chart performance
Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
"Need You Now" has received critical acclaim from music critics and is considered one of the best country songs of the 2000s. It won the 2011 Grammy Award for Record of the Year and Song of the Year.

The song received a "thumbs up" review from [[Jim Malec]] of the 9513. He said that although Charles Kelley's voice had a "surprisingly stuffy tone," lead singer Hillary Scott's voice fit perfectly for "dark" songs like "Need You Now." He said that both singers had a rawness in their voices that made the song feel "real".<ref name="the9513">{{cite web |url=http://www.the9513.com/lady-antebellum-need-you-now/ |title=Lady Antebellum – "Need You Now" |last=Malec |first=Jim |date=August 17, 2009 |access-date=August 27, 2009 |work=The 9513|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131102102353/http://www.the9513.com/lady-antebellum-need-you-now/|archive-date=November 2, 2013}}</ref>

The track received a positive review from Ken Tucker of ''Billboard'', who said, "the song finds alto Scott trading lead vocals with a soulful Kelley, and it will connect with anyone who's ever dumped a significant other and regretted it in the early morning hours."<ref>{{cite magazine| url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/review/1070904/lady-antebellum-need-you-know| title=Lady Antebellum, "Need You Know"| last=Tucker| first=Ken| date=September 3, 2009| access-date=March 15, 2013| magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]}}</ref>

Bobby Peacock of ''Roughstock'' gave a positive review as well, comparing its sound favorably to that of "[[I Run to You]]." He also thought the traded-off lead vocals gave the song "more depth," and that Kelley and Scott sang more strongly than on the debut album.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roughstock.com/blog/lady-antebellum-need-you-now- |title=Lady Antebellum — "Need You Now" |author=Bobby Peacock |date=August 13, 2009 |work=Roughstock |access-date=October 16, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090923221302/http://www.roughstock.com/blog/lady-antebellum-need-you-now- |archive-date=September 23, 2009 }}</ref>

Critics in Europe and North America have pointed to similarities between "Need You Now" and "[[Eye in the Sky (song)|Eye in the Sky]]" by [[the Alan Parsons Project]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Rodgers D. |first=Patrick|url=http://www.nashvillescene.com/nashvillecream/archives/2010/11/11/alan-parsons-camp-alleges-lady-antebellum-rip-off |title=Alan Parsons' Camp Alleges Lady Antebellum Rip-Off|work= Nashville Scene |date=November 11, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111107191303/http://www.nashvillescene.com/nashvillecream/archives/2010/11/11/alan-parsons-camp-alleges-lady-antebellum-rip-off|archive-date=November 7, 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Is this an Awards Show or What?|url=http://www.nowtoronto.com/daily/music/story.cfm?content=179164|newspaper=NOW Toronto|date=February 14, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714203803/https://nowtoronto.com/daily/music/story.cfm?content=179164|archive-date=July 14, 2011 }}</ref>
sections.text:
"Need You Now" has received critical acclaim from music critics and is considered one of the best country songs of the 2000s. It won the 2011 Grammy Award for Record of the Year and Song of the Year.

The song received a "thumbs up" review from Jim Malec of the 9513. He said that although Charles Kelley's voice had a "surprisingly stuffy tone," lead singer Hillary Scott's voice fit perfectly for "dark" songs like "Need You Now." He said that both singers had a rawness in their voices that made the song feel "real".

The track received a positive review from Ken Tucker of Billboard, who said, "the song finds alto Scott trading lead vocals with a soulful Kelley, and it will connect with anyone who's ever dumped a significant other and regretted it in the early morning hours."

Bobby Peacock of Roughstock gave a positive review as well, comparing its sound favorably to that of "I Run to You." He also thought the traded-off lead vocals gave the song "more depth," and that Kelley and Scott sang more strongly than on the debut album.

Critics in Europe and North America have pointed to similarities between "Need You Now" and "Eye in the Sky" by the Alan Parsons Project.

sections.heading: Cover versions and live performances
sections.wikitext:
In December 2010, [[Adele]] and [[Darius Rucker]] performed the song at the [[CMT (American TV channel)|CMT]] Artists of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Adele And Maroon 5 Add A Pop Twist To CMT Artist Of The Year Performances|url=http://idolator.com/5708352/adele-maroon-5-cmt-artist-of-the-year-performances|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411025541/http://idolator.com/5708352/adele-maroon-5-cmt-artist-of-the-year-performances|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 11, 2013|publisher=[[Idolator (website)|Idolator]]|access-date=February 21, 2013|date=December 5, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Adele and Darius Rucker: Better Than Lady Antebellum?|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/speakeasy/2010/12/06/adele-and-darius-rucker-better-than-lady-antebellum/|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|access-date=February 21, 2013|date=December 6, 2010}}</ref>

In February 2011, [[Lea Michele]] and [[Mark Salling]] covered the song during the [[glee season 2|second season]] of [[Glee (TV series)|Glee]] during the episode [[The Sue Sylvester Shuffle]].

[[Gary Barlow]] and [[Cheryl (singer)|Cheryl]] performed the song at the [[Diamond Jubilee Concert]] at [[Buckingham Palace]] on June 4, 2012.{{citation needed|date=January 2025}}

Mia Silva performed a Portuguese-language cover version entitled "Preciso de Voce" on her 2011 album ''Saudade Magoa''.

In 2017, [[Shane Filan]] of [[Westlife]] included a version of the song on his album ''[[Love Always (Shane Filan album)|Love Always]]''. This was released as a promotional single in East Asia (with a new arrangement and a duet with Filipino [[bossa nova]] artist [[Sitti]]), and it charted on [[iTunes]] Top Songs in Laos, the Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam, Cambodia, and Malaysia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://magicmusicmagazine.com/2018/02/08/shanefilan-4/|title = New Single : Need You Now (Lady Antebellum)- Shane Filan & Sitti|date = February 8, 2018}}</ref>
sections.text:
In December 2010, Adele and Darius Rucker performed the song at the CMT Artists of the Year.

In February 2011, Lea Michele and Mark Salling covered the song during the second season of Glee during the episode The Sue Sylvester Shuffle.

Gary Barlow and Cheryl performed the song at the Diamond Jubilee Concert at Buckingham Palace on June 4, 2012.{{citation needed|date=January 2025}}

Mia Silva performed a Portuguese-language cover version entitled "Preciso de Voce" on her 2011 album Saudade Magoa.

In 2017, Shane Filan of Westlife included a version of the song on his album Love Always. This was released as a promotional single in East Asia (with a new arrangement and a duet with Filipino bossa nova artist Sitti), and it charted on iTunes Top Songs in Laos, the Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam, Cambodia, and Malaysia.
